class_id: a completion condition that a timer keeps re-arming never completes
feature: any job, slot, batch or queue that declares itself done when its due set is empty, where membership of the due set is decided by elapsed time (a retry-after, backoff, next-due or TTL stamp) rather than by an event that happens once
symptom: a run is 'complete' only when nothing is due, but an item becomes due again merely because time passed. When the re-arm interval is shorter than or comparable to the time the run needs to drain its due set (wakes 30 minutes apart, a 30/60-minute retry, a per-wake cap), every continuation finds the same items due again, spends its budget on them, and ends 'incomplete'. Nothing throws and every single attempt is individually correct; the aggregate never converges. The same shape appears when a fix removes the timer but keeps an item permanently eligible under a different rule (for example 'every open row once per slot' with a per-wake cap smaller than the backlog): the completion condition is still unreachable, only more slowly. The generic test is a convergence test on the REAL due-computation: N items, cap C per wake, no new events -> after ceil(N/C) wakes the due set is empty and the run logs complete, and each item was attempted exactly once. A timer-based or always-eligible rule fails it.
first_seen: 2026-09-23/24 -- IPODhan #943. F-151: on staging the 00:00 IST data slot never logged complete; the document state machine re-armed every open document_fetch_state row on a 30/60-minute or 6-hour timer while wakes are 30 minutes apart, so each continuation wake re-found the same documents due and exhausted the 60 s discovery budget. F-152: the field-plan walk wrote a doubling 15 min - 6 h backoff and logged structural gaps as TRANSIENT. PR #957 round 1 removed the timer but made LISTED rows 'due once per slot' and dropped LISTED deferral from the completion condition; the Tier A review measured staging (LISTED document_fetch_state: BLOCKED_ALL 202 rows / 52 IPOs) and showed that at cap 2 per wake one pass needs 26 wakes while a slot has 16, so 'every LISTED row once per slot' could never complete a slot either.
fix_prs: PR #957 round 2: due-ness is event-based, never elapsed-time. An open row is attempted at most once per OD-19 data slot (next_retry_at holds only a slot start); a LISTED IPO's open row is attempted ONCE after the IPO entered LISTED (new column document_fetch_state.attempted_at_stage, migration 0054, written only by a concluded chain) and again only when a new document row or a document first seen after its last attempt appears (OD-56, OD-81 event 2). Due LISTED work is back in the slot completion condition. Convergence test (52 IPOs cap 2, 7 cap 2, 10 cap 3) asserts complete at wake ceil(N/C)-1 and exactly one attempt per IPO; mutation 'LISTED rows due every slot' turns 5 of 7 tests red.
detection_check: the staging wake log's per-slot complete/incomplete line (document cycle summary `slotComplete` / `incompletePasses`) read by the proof: a slot that never logs complete across its wakes is this class. No nightly audit check yet; the general property is a convergence unit test on any due-computation that gates a completion flag.
